bull.b: Having three programs in Phase III creates multiple potential regulatory and commercial opportunities across retinitis pigmentosa, Stargardt disease, and geographic atrophy. This diversified late-stage pipeline may reduce reliance on a single asset and provides several milestone paths over the next two years.

A platform that can address many genetic causes with one therapy could broaden the treatable patient population beyond a mutation-specific model. If clinical and regulatory progress continues, this approach may support repeatable development opportunities across multiple retinal diseases.

The OCU400 licensing agreement expands regional access while preserving potential milestone and royalty economics for Ocugen. Partner-led development and commercialization can provide external infrastructure and validation, while manufacturing supply arrangements may support future recurring participation.

bear.b: Large and persistent operating losses show that Ocugen has not yet demonstrated operating leverage despite modest revenue improvement. Continued losses could require additional financing before product revenue becomes meaningful, increasing execution pressure as several programs advance toward filings.

Negative equity combined with sharply higher debt weakens financial flexibility and increases the burden on future financing or partnering outcomes. This capital structure may constrain investment across the pipeline and leave the company more exposed if development timelines or approvals extend.

Cash coverage for only two of three late-stage programs creates a structural prioritization risk as all assets require continued clinical and regulatory investment. Unless additional funding or partnerships are secured, one program may face slower progress, reduced scope, or dependence on future capital.
